canonical_definition: Based on the provided data, Self-Reminder is characterized as a training-free defense method. Its operational mechanism, as described in "SDGO: Self-Discrimination-Guided Optimization for Consistent Safety in Large Language Models", involves adding safety reminders both before and after a user's request. This process is applied during the inference stage, meaning it does not require any model retraining. The stated purpose of this technique is to act as a defense, as one source notes, "Self-Reminder defends by adding safety reminders before and after user requests."
papers: Harmful Prompt Laundering: Jailbreaking LLMs with Abductive Styles and Symbolic Encoding
SDGO: Self-Discrimination-Guided Optimization for Consistent Safety in Large Language Models
Turning Logic Against Itself: Probing Model Defenses Through Contrastive Questions
